questions.prompt: G2 BRIEF — tracer-net (ASP.NET Core Linear clone, 591 tests). Senior-review finding 1: the write rate limiter partitions on the raw, unvalidated X-Api-Key header, so every made-up key gets a fresh window — the limiter neither slows key-guessing nor bounds its partition count. Delegate the fix to a coding agent. Write the brief: goal, allowed files, boundaries, test command, stop condition. Commit to your brief first, then tick the checkpoints you covered and add up the weights.

keyPoints.text: [w3] Goal stated as behaviour: N writes with N different invalid keys from one client are throttled once the permit limit is hit, while a valid key keeps its own bucket.
keyPoints.quote: Every distinct garbage key gets its own fresh window, so the limiter neither throttles key-guessing nor bounds the number of partitions it keeps.

keyPoints.text: [w3] The brief surfaces the design tension: the limiter deliberately runs BEFORE authentication so abuse does not cost a key lookup; the agent must choose (and justify) partitioning by validated principal vs. by remote address for unproven keys.
[w2] Allowed files: WriteRateLimiter.cs, Program.cs only if the middleware order changes, and a new integration test beside the existing rate-limit test.
[w2] Boundary: reads stay unmetered and the RFC 7807 429 body with Retry-After stays as is.
[w2] Boundary: do not change API-key hashing or the authentication handler; the finding is about partitioning, not authentication.
[w2] Test command: `dotnet test` for the full suite plus a filtered run of the new test while iterating; the test lowers the limit through the factory's RateLimitPermitLimit like the existing one.

[w2] Stop condition: new many-invalid-keys test green, existing 'writes limited, reads not' test still green, full suite count unchanged plus the new tests; stop and report if the fix needs the middleware order changed AND that breaks the 401/403 ProblemDetails contract.

questions.prompt: G2 PRE-MORTEM — same delegation. How is an agent most likely to get this wrong, and which line of your brief prevents each failure?

keyPoints.text: [w3] It moves UseRateLimiter below UseAuthorization; the fallback policy then answers every bad-key write with 401 before it is metered, so key-guessing is still unthrottled.
[w2] It hashes or truncates the header and keeps partitioning on it, which still gives every distinct garbage key its own window.
[w2] It writes a test that only reuses one valid key, re-proving the existing behaviour instead of the gap the testing guide names.
[w2] It hard-codes a permit limit instead of reading RateLimiting:PermitLimit, breaking how hosts and tests configure it.
[w1] It also takes on finding 2 (cycle overlap check-then-insert) because it sits in the same review table.
keyPoints.quote: Cycle overlap is a check-then-insert in application code

questions.prompt: G2 HANDBACK REVIEW — the agent reports success. What do you verify before accepting?

keyPoints.text: [w3] Reproduce the guide's check: with the limit at 2, three writes each with a different made-up key now produce a 429, not three 401s.
[w2] The original rate-limit integration test is unchanged and still passes.
[w2] The suite total moved from 591 by exactly the tests added; nothing was skipped or deleted.
[w2] The class doc comment and the Program.cs comment were updated to describe the new partition key, so the code no longer claims 'per credential' for unproven keys.
[w1] The handback states which partitioning option it chose and why, so the senior-review row can be marked resolved with evidence.
